body:
Source: GitHub issues #728 and #732.
1. (#728) In packages/prosecute/bin/adlc-prosecute.mjs, tier-check calls resolveProsecutionRevision({ dir: values.dir, base: values.base, revision: values.revision }) without passing input / inputPath: values.input, whereas record-cross-model reads values.input and passes { input, inputPath: values.input }. When a tracked evidence packet (e.g. .adlc/passes.json) is modified in the working tree and passed via --input, record-cross-model excludes it from the revision digest while tier-check includes it, so tier-check can never match the recorded attestation.
2. (#732) In packages/prosecute/bin/adlc-prosecute.mjs, the non-JSON failure exit branch prints console.error(result.message) unconditionally even when runProsecution returns an op-error object with no message field, emitting a literal "undefined" line to stderr before result.errors.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- AC1: When --input <path> is passed to tier-check, read and parse the JSON file (calling opError on read/parse failure just like record-cross-model) and pass input and inputPath: values.input to resolveProsecutionRevision so tier-check resolves the identical git-change:<base>:<digest> revision as record-cross-model.
- AC2: Guard console.error(result.message) on the failure exit path in packages/prosecute/bin/adlc-prosecute.mjs so unset result.message does not print "undefined" to stderr.
- AC3: Unit/CLI tests in packages/prosecute/test/prosecute-tier-check-cli.test.mjs and packages/prosecute/test/prosecute-cli.test.mjs verify both behaviors and kill all mutants.
title: prosecute: thread --input into tier-check revision resolution and guard unset result.message on op-error exits (#728, #732)
